name: De Burghs Bridge
facts: De Burghs Bridge opened on 15 December 1967, replacing the 1901 timber truss that was the longest single timber truss span ever built in Australia at 50 metres.
The current six‑lane concrete bridge runs perpendicular to the river, a stark contrast to the winding approach roads of the original timber bridge, showcasing 1960s engineering progress.
A plaque on the bridge, installed in 1988, commemorates the original 1901 bridge even after its 1994 bushfire destruction, leaving visible abutments as a historical reminder.
